results.summary_before: This is a current-controlled 4-stage differential ring VCO in SKY130 with buffered rail-to-rail outputs providing four quadrature phases at 45 degree spacing. Frequency is set by an external control current mirrored into the PFET loads and NFET tail sources of each stage, with a tuning range of roughly 200 kHz to 3 MHz. One analog pin takes the control current and another exposes the internal bias voltage for monitoring. Testing requires a current source or resistor network plus an oscilloscope or frequency counter, and the design is based on a published reference circuit.

results.summary_before: Basic8 is a minimal 8-bit CPU with 8 general-purpose registers, an ALU supporting arithmetic, logic, and shift operations, and branch and jump instructions. Instructions are 16 bits wide and are loaded in two cycles via the input pins, with the program counter output on the output pins to allow an external controller to feed instructions from a ROM. The design is tested with a cocotb testbench covering the full instruction set. No external hardware is required, as the CPU is driven entirely through the pins.

results.summary_before: This design implements a complete Blackjack card game in Verilog for a 1x1 Tiny Tapeout tile. It uses a finite state machine to manage game flow, an LFSR for card randomness, and outputs game status via LEDs and a 3-bit sum to a 7-segment display. The game is controlled by hit and stand buttons, with win/lose/push indicated by LEDs. External hardware needed includes a clock source, push buttons, LEDs, and a 7-segment display; button debouncing is optional.

results.summary_before: TinyFarm is a hardware farming game implemented in SystemVerilog that maintains four fields with crops that grow, can be watered, and are harvested to fulfill customer orders. Player inputs select mode, field, and crop and trigger actions, while a VGA output in RGB222 format displays the farm grid and game status. The design needs a Tiny VGA PMOD and a monitor to view the output, plus buttons or switches for the control inputs. It originated as a university final project and is notable for fitting a small game with inventory and order logic into a single tile pair.

results.summary_before: This project is a simple 8-bit, single-cycle processor with a RISC-V-style instruction set and an accumulator-based data path. It has no internal instruction memory; the 16-bit instruction is applied externally through the 8 input pins and 8 bidirectional pins. Testing requires driving those pins with switches, an MCU, or an FPGA, and the design is intended for educational use or small embedded control logic. The documentation notes that manual switch input is impractical, so an external microcontroller such as an ESP32 is recommended.

results.summary_before: This is a compact 8-bit teaching CPU with four general registers, a 24x8 data RAM, an 8-bit ALU and a 16-instruction ISA. Instructions are supplied externally on the eight input pins, with the destination register value on the outputs and PC, zero, carry and fetch-phase flags on the bidirectional pins for debugging. It is intended as an educational design, with unit tests for the ALU, control FSM, registers, memory and datapath, and it needs external memory to hold instructions. The design is configured for a 1x2 tile footprint and has no on-chip program ROM.
